meta_description:
4,259 likes, 23 comments - bonappetitmag on October 30, 2026: "Some legacy is etched in stone. Some is baked to perfection. In "To Die For," archivist Rosie Grant (@ghostly.archive) visits cemeteries nationwide to preserve a rare kind of family heritage: recipes carved directly onto headstones. 

From Texas meatloaf to Reddit-famous spritz cookies in Brooklyn, Grant tracks down the families of the departed, and with their permission, cooks the dishes they left as their legacy, in order to honor the ordinary people who fed their communities. More than a cookbook, "To Die For" is a feel-good gateway into conversations about death, writes @jessitaylorro. For Grant, sitting around the table to share a meal or stepping into a memory-filled kitchen help disintegrate emotional barriers.

What recipe would you take to the grave? Read more at the link in bio.".
